place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 大比 · 对秦雁
place.en: Chending Temple · The contest · Against Qin Yan

setup.zh: 第三轮，对面是内门的秦雁：八层，真灵根，使剑，一口下阶的法器，人在一丈开外，剑气已到了跟前。前两回大比，两回打进前四，两回都输在祁长松手上；她八层卡了两年，要那颗筑基丹筑基：「我不让你。你也别让我。」
setup.en: Round three, and across from you is Qin Yan of the inner sect: eighth layer, true root, a sword — a low-grade magic treasure; she's a zhang off and the sword's breath is already on you. In the last two contests she made the last four both times and lost to Qi Changsong both times; stuck at the eighth layer for two years, she wants that Foundation pill to lay her foundation: "I won't give way to you. Don't you give way to me."

recap.zh: 第三轮你对秦雁：她的剑，她的冰锥，你土墙挡冰，火打脚；二十招里，你一步一步往西北角那摊红油上挪。三十招上她把你逼到台边，袖子里的雷符始终没掏——剑尖往前一送，你迎了上去，剑上的青气从肘弯犁到肩头；你一把攥住她的剑鞘。她那一掌收了三分，你脚下一勾，她的脚跟踩在油上，溜出了台沿。
recap.en: In round three you fought Qin Yan: against her sword and her ice spikes you raised earth walls to stop the ice and threw fire at her feet; for twenty moves you edged step by step toward the patch of red oil in the north-west corner. At the thirtieth move she drove you to the edge, the thunder talisman in her sleeve never drawn — the point came forward and you stepped into it; the green light on the blade ploughed from your elbow to your shoulder; you seized her scabbard. She pulled a third of her palm; you hooked her foot, her heel came down on the oil, and she slid off the edge of the stage.

en: Second in the inner sect: Qin Yan, eighth layer.
"I won't give way to you. Don't you give way to me."

story.zh:
第三轮，马小宝对鲁泥鳅。鲁泥鳅上台前，从小满身边挤过去，压低了嗓子：「那面镜子，是我爹的船从下邳捎上来的。红布底下，半夜里自己亮过一回——冷的，像泗水底下的光。我爹说，那不是照妖的，是认东西的。」

那面镜子，不是一举就亮的。马小宝两手捧着它，脸上的斑「腾」地一红，像是有人往他身子里抽东西，抽出来，灌进镜子里——镜面这才亮了。照到第三回，鲁泥鳅一脚踩空，跌下了台。

小满对的，是秦雁。

台角的水缸边上，两个人碰上了。秦雁望着台上那炷香，「你知道我为什么非拿这个头名不可？」小满摇头。秦雁道：「头名那颗筑基丹。我八层卡了两年了。我爹前年叫熊把腿咬了，躺到如今。」她顿了一顿，「境界上去了，别的都好办。上不去，什么都办不了。」她把瓢放回缸沿上，看着他，「我不让你。你也别让我。」

小满跟着上了台。[秦雁]{注=neimen-shijie}比他高半个头，两道眉毛长而直，像两口出了鞘的剑。她平日不大笑，一张脸冷冷的。秦雁道：「沈师弟，听说你只有四层。」小满道：「是，只有四层。」秦雁道：「我说过，不让。」小满道：「我打不过，会跑的。」秦雁一愣，随即笑了，嘴角露出一颗虎牙，跟那张冷脸怎么也对不上，倒比不笑的时候好看。
story.en:
In the third round, Ma Xiaobao faced Lu the Loach. Before going up, Lu the Loach squeezed past Xiaoman and said under his breath: "That mirror came up from Xiapi on my pa's boat. Under a red cloth, in the middle of the night, it lit up by itself once. Cold, like the light at the bottom of the Si. My pa says it's not for showing demons. It's for recognising things."

That mirror didn't light the moment it was raised. Ma Xiaobao held it in both hands, and the blotches on his face flushed red all at once, as if something were being drawn out of his body, drawn out and poured into the mirror. Only then did the mirror's face light. At the third shining, Lu the Loach put a foot on nothing and fell off the stage.

Xiaoman's opponent was Qin Yan.

By the water vat at the stage's corner, the two of them met. Qin Yan was watching the incense stick on the stage. "Do you know why I have to have first place?" Xiaoman shook his head. Qin Yan said: "The first-place Foundation Pill. I've been stuck at eighth layer two years. The year before last a bear bit my pa's leg, and he's been lying in bed ever since." She paused. "Get your realm up, and everything else is easy. Don't, and you can't do anything." She set the ladle back on the vat's rim and looked at him. "I won't give way to you. Don't you give way to me either."

Xiaoman followed her up. [Qin Yan]{注=neimen-shijie} was half a head taller than him, her two eyebrows long and straight, like two swords out of their scabbards. On ordinary days she didn't smile much, and her face was cool. Qin Yan said: "Junior Brother Shen, I hear you're only fourth layer." Xiaoman said: "Yes, only fourth layer." Qin Yan said: "I told you. I won't give way." Xiaoman said: "If I can't win, I'll run." Qin Yan was taken aback, then laughed, a little pointed eyetooth showing at the corner of her mouth that didn't match that cool face at all, and was prettier than when she didn't smile.

story_full.zh:
第三轮，马小宝对鲁泥鳅。鲁泥鳅上台前，从小满身边挤过去，压低了嗓子：「昨儿我下山去船上看我爹。那面镜子，是我爹的船从下邳捎上来的——马三老爷雇的是我爹的船——在我爹船舱里搁了一路。红布底下，半夜里自己亮过一回——冷的，像泗水底下的光。我爹说，那不是照妖的，是认东西的。」说完，他搓了搓手，上台去了。鲁泥鳅是渔户的儿子，水性好，身子滑，头一拳便钻到了马小宝腋下。马小宝这才摘下了铜镜。

小满站在台下，看得清清楚楚：那面镜子，不是一举就亮的。马小宝两手捧着它，脸上的斑「腾」地一红，一片一片鼓起来，像是有人往他身子里抽东西，抽出来，灌进镜子里——镜面这才亮了，一道黄光扑在鲁泥鳅脸上。鲁泥鳅「哎哟」一声，捂着眼睛倒退，嘴里直叫：「冷的！那光是冷的，往心口钻！」他退一步，马小宝又照一回，斑又红一回，喘得两个肩膀一耸一耸；照到第三回，鲁泥鳅一脚踩空，跌下了台。马小宝捧着镜子，站在那里喘了好一会儿，才喘匀。他冲台下的小满扬了扬下巴。

小满对的，是秦雁。

台角的水缸边上，两个人碰上了。秦雁舀了半瓢水，没喝，递给了他。小满接过来喝了，道：「秦师姐。秘境里那一回……」秦雁道：「你没往下坠。我记得。」她又舀了一瓢，自己喝了，望着台上那炷香，「你知道我为什么非拿这个头名不可？」小满摇头。秦雁道：「头名那颗筑基丹。我八层卡了两年了。我爹前年叫熊把腿咬了，躺到如今，凡药接不上；坊市上有接得上的，三道纹的回春丹，一颗二百块灵石，我一月的份例是十块。筑了基，这些都不算事——筑基的师叔开口，丹房肯赊；练气的开口，没人听。」她顿了一顿，「境界上去了，别的都好办。上不去，什么都办不了。」她把瓢放回缸沿上，看着他，「我不让你。你也别让我。」

小满捧着那瓢，半天没说出话来。他把瓢放下。秦雁点了点头，先上了台。

小满跟着上了台。[秦雁]{注=neimen-shijie}比他高半个头，两道眉毛长而直，像两口出了鞘的剑，从来没描过；脸上一点脂粉也不搽，干干净净的，透着山里姑娘的那股精神气。她平日不大笑，一张脸冷冷的。她一上台，台下内门那一片，先静了一半。小满先看的却是她的脚：站得真稳，脚底下像钉了钉子。秦雁道：「沈师弟，听说你只有四层。」小满道：「是，只有四层。」秦雁道：「我说过，不让。」小满道：「我打不过，会跑的。」秦雁一愣，随即笑了，嘴角露出一颗虎牙，跟那张冷脸怎么也对不上，倒比不笑的时候好看。
story_full.en:
In the third round, Ma Xiaobao faced Lu the Loach. Before going up, Lu the Loach squeezed past Xiaoman and said under his breath: "Yesterday I went down the mountain to see my pa on his boat. That mirror came up from Xiapi on my pa's boat; Master Ma San hired my pa's boat. It sat in my pa's cabin the whole way. Under a red cloth, in the middle of the night, it lit up by itself once. Cold, like the light at the bottom of the Si. My pa says it's not for showing demons. It's for recognising things." Having said it, he rubbed his hands and went up. Lu the Loach was a fisherman's son, a good swimmer, slippery-bodied, and with his first punch he'd ducked in under Ma Xiaobao's armpit. Only then did Ma Xiaobao take off the copper mirror.

Xiaoman stood below the stage and saw it plainly: that mirror didn't light the moment it was raised. Ma Xiaobao held it in both hands, and the blotches on his face flushed red all at once and swelled up patch by patch, as if something were being drawn out of his body, drawn out and poured into the mirror. Only then did the mirror's face light, and a beam of yellow light struck Lu the Loach in the face. Lu the Loach cried out and backed away with his hands over his eyes, yelling: "It's cold! The light's cold, it goes into your heart!" Each step he backed, Ma Xiaobao shone it again, and the blotches flushed again, and he panted till both his shoulders heaved. At the third shining, Lu the Loach put a foot on nothing and fell off the stage. Ma Xiaobao stood there holding the mirror, panting a good while before he got his breath even. He lifted his chin at Xiaoman below.

Xiaoman's opponent was Qin Yan.

By the water vat at the stage's corner, the two of them met. Qin Yan scooped half a ladle of water, didn't drink it, and handed it to him. Xiaoman took it and drank, and said: "Senior Sister Qin. That time in the secret realm..." Qin Yan said: "You didn't hang on it. I remember." She scooped another ladle and drank it herself, watching the incense stick on the stage. "Do you know why I have to have first place?" Xiaoman shook his head. Qin Yan said: "The first-place Foundation Pill. I've been stuck at eighth layer two years. The year before last a bear bit my pa's leg, and he's been lying in bed ever since; ordinary medicine can't mend it. At the market there's medicine that can: a Spring-Return Pill of three lines, two hundred spirit stones each, and my monthly allowance is ten. Once I've established my foundation, none of that counts. When a martial uncle of Foundation Establishment asks, the pill house will give credit; when a Qi Condensation disciple asks, nobody listens." She paused. "Get your realm up, and everything else is easy. Don't, and you can't do anything." She set the ladle back on the vat's rim and looked at him. "I won't give way to you. Don't you give way to me either."

Xiaoman held the ladle and for a long while couldn't say anything. He put the ladle down. Qin Yan nodded and went up on the stage first.

Xiaoman followed her up. [Qin Yan]{注=neimen-shijie} was half a head taller than him, her two eyebrows long and straight, like two swords out of their scabbards, never once pencilled; not a trace of powder on her face, clean as clean, with the brisk spirit of a mountain girl about her. On ordinary days she didn't smile much, and her face was cool. The moment she came on the stage, half of the inner sect below went quiet first. But what Xiaoman looked at first was her feet: she stood truly steady, as if her soles were nailed down. Qin Yan said: "Junior Brother Shen, I hear you're only fourth layer." Xiaoman said: "Yes, only fourth layer." Qin Yan said: "I told you. I won't give way." Xiaoman said: "If I can't win, I'll run." Qin Yan was taken aback, then laughed, a little pointed eyetooth showing at the corner of her mouth that didn't match that cool face at all, and was prettier than when she didn't smile.

label.en: Watch her feet; last thirty moves

exits.means: fights Qin Yan, outlasting her moves while edging toward the spilt tallow; at the edge steps into her thrust — its edge-light ploughs his left arm open — seizes her scabbard, hooks her back foot as she pulls her palm, and her heel slides on the oil off the stage

say.zh: 相克：对面的冰锥来了，立一堵土墙，全扎在土里——「水得土而绝」。
say.en: What eats what: when the ice spikes come, an earth wall takes them all — "water is stopped by earth."

say.zh: 阿禾的底册：秦雁，剑气三尺。到了台边，往前送一寸。出手留三分。不踩人。
say.en: Ahe's records: Qin Yan — sword-qi three feet. At the edge, one inch more. Holds back three parts. Never stamps.

goal.zh: 三十招：看她的脚，在台上撑过七个回合，便算过了。
goal.en: Thirty moves: watch her feet and stand seven turns on the stage, and you have passed.

game._foe: 三十招 (第六回): 撑过她七个回合便算过 —— 打不穿她 (hp 6)。2026-10-16 起得牌都在剧情里、银月不上台，牌少了：她的寒潭两张换成水雾、一只鹿影换成水雾 (lookahead 57%)。

withdrawn.zh: 秦雁把剑收回半寸，退后一步：「再来。」
withdrawn.en: Qin Yan draws her sword back half an inch and steps back. "Again."

story.zh:
这一场，跟方才那一场大不一样。秦雁的剑是真剑，招是真招——剑尖递出去，剑上那一道青气还要往前再走三尺。小满不看她的剑，看她的脚。第七招，剑尖挑破了他的袖子；第十五招，挑破了他的肩头；第二十招上，一道血口子从他右颊上拉过去。

可他没有乱躲。东一跳，西一滚，二十招里，他往台子的西北角上挪了七步。那一角的台沿上，有一摊红油，花椒粒子还粘在石缝里。

第二十二招上，三根冰锥齐齐射了过来。小满一掌按在青石板上，身前拱起一片土墙；另一只手里已经冒出一团火，朝她脚底下打过去。台下有人叫起来：「两样！又是两样！」

可躲着躲着，小满觉出一样东西来，是他打记事起没有过的：他在笑。这是头一回，对面站着一个比他强的人，一招一招都是真的，不藏，不让，不图他什么。

三十招上，他到底给逼到了台边——他自己挑的那一段台边。左脚边上一尺，便是那摊油。秦雁的剑尖，抵在了他喉咙上，凉丝丝的。秦雁右手的袖子里，一直扣着一张黄纸雷符，始终没有掏出来。她往台下看了一眼：头一排蹲着几个刚进门的小孩子。那张符，她没有掏。

小满没有退。剑尖往前一送的那一霎，他往前迎了上去——身子一侧，让过喉咙，人贴着剑脊撞了进去。剑上那道青气从他左臂外侧犁过去，从肘弯一直犁到肩头。他拿那只淌着血的左手，一把攥住了她左手里那截剑鞘。

秦雁一惊。她撒了鞘，左掌一翻，掌心里亮起一层青光。大比不许伤人性命。那层青光亮了一亮，她收了三分。小满等的就是她收的这一下。她的后脚边上，是那摊红油。他脚下一勾——猎户下套子勾兔子腿的那一下。那一掌到底印了上来，只剩下三分，印在他胸口上，撞着一块硬东西，是烫的。

秦雁的脚跟，踩在了油上。鞋底「哧」地一溜，溜出了台沿。她落在了台下的冻土上，站着落的，剑还在手里。执事咽了一口唾沫，敲锣：「……秦雁出台。沈小满，胜。」

小满爬起来，把那截剑鞘双手递了下去。秦雁接过鞘，道：「你是把我往那摊油上领的。」小满道：「……是，师姐。」秦雁道：「你是从第几招起，往那边领的？」小满道：「从头一招起。」又道：「往油上领人——猎户的套子。」小满一怔：「师姐怎么知道？」秦雁道：「我爹也是打猎的。我这个名字，就是他起的——他说雁是天上最难射的东西，一辈子没射着过一只。」她说着，竟笑了一笑，「他要是看见今天这一场，准说：那小子，拿一条胳膊换一只雁。」

秘境里伸进坑里拉他上来的，就是方才递回去的那一截剑鞘。她转身要走，又停住了，背对着他，声音压得低低的：「四强，你跟马小宝一个半边。你怀里揣着的，不管是什么，捂紧了。」

老槐树底下，钱掌柜拿炭条把木板上的名字划得只剩几行：**祁长松　一赔一。马小宝　一赔四。**沈小满那一行，他把「二十」抹了，写上一个「五」。有人挤上来嚷：「掌柜的，我晌午押的是二十！」钱掌柜眼皮也不抬：「押出去的，照押出去的算。」
story.en:
This bout was nothing like the one before. Qin Yan's sword was a real sword and her moves were real moves. When the point went out, a streak of green qi on the blade went on another three feet. Xiaoman didn't watch her sword. He watched her feet. At the seventh move the point slit his sleeve; at the fifteenth it slit his shoulder; at the twentieth a cut ran across his right cheek.

But he wasn't dodging at random. A jump this way, a roll that, and in twenty moves he had worked seven steps towards the north-west corner of the stage. On the stage's edge at that corner was a slick of red oil, Sichuan peppercorns still stuck in the cracks.

At the twenty-second move, three ice spikes shot at him together. Xiaoman slapped a palm onto the bluestone and a patch of earth wall heaved up in front of him. In his other hand a ball of fire had already come up, and he threw it at her feet. Someone below cried out: "Two! Two again!"

But dodging and dodging, Xiaoman felt something he had never had since he could remember: he was smiling. This was the first time someone stronger than him stood facing him, every move real, nothing hidden, nothing given way, wanting nothing from him.

At the thirtieth move he was forced at last to the stage's edge. The stretch of edge he had chosen himself. A foot from his left foot was that slick of oil. The point of Qin Yan's sword rested against his throat, cool. Up the right sleeve of Qin Yan's robe, all this time, she had been holding a yellow paper thunder talisman. She had never brought it out. She looked down off the stage: crouched in the front row were a few small children just come into the sect. She didn't bring that talisman out.

Xiaoman didn't step back. In the instant the point pushed forward, he went forward to meet it: body turned sideways to let it past his throat, he drove in along the flat of the blade. The green qi on the sword ploughed along the outside of his left arm, from the crook of the elbow right up to the shoulder. With his bleeding left hand, he seized the length of scabbard in her left hand.

Qin Yan started. She let go of the scabbard and turned her left palm up, and a layer of green light lit in it. The contest forbade taking life. The green light flared once, and she held back three tenths. That holding back was what Xiaoman had been waiting for. Beside her rear foot was that slick of red oil. His foot hooked out (the move a hunter uses to hook a hare's leg into a snare). The palm did land in the end, with only three tenths left, pressed onto his chest, and struck something hard there that was hot.

Qin Yan's heel came down on the oil. Her sole went skidding, *tsss*, off the edge of the stage. She landed on the frozen ground below the stage, landed standing, sword still in hand. The steward swallowed and struck the gong: "...Qin Yan is off the stage. Shen Xiaoman wins."

Xiaoman got up and handed the length of scabbard down to her with both hands. Qin Yan took the scabbard and said: "You led me onto that oil." Xiaoman said: "...Yes, Senior Sister." Qin Yan said: "From which move did you start leading me there?" Xiaoman said: "From the first." Then she said: "Leading someone onto oil. A hunter's snare." Xiaoman started: "How do you know, Senior Sister?" Qin Yan said: "My pa's a hunter too. He gave me my name. He says the wild goose is the hardest thing in the sky to shoot, and he never shot one in his life." As she said it, she actually smiled. "If he'd seen this bout today, he'd say for sure: that lad traded an arm for a goose."

In the secret realm, what had reached down into the pit to pull him up was the very length of scabbard he'd just handed back. She turned to go, then stopped, her back to him, her voice pitched low: "Last four, you and Ma Xiaobao are in the same half. Whatever it is you've got in your robe, keep a tight hold of it."

Under the old pagoda tree, Shopkeeper Qian had crossed out names on the board with his charcoal until only a few lines were left: **Qi Changsong · evens. Ma Xiaobao · four to one.** On Shen Xiaoman's line he rubbed out "twenty" and wrote a "five." Somebody pushed up shouting: "Shopkeeper, I bet at twenty at noon!" Shopkeeper Qian didn't lift an eyelid: "What's been bet goes at what it was bet at."

story_full.zh:
这一场，跟方才那一场大不一样。秦雁的剑是真剑，招是真招——那是一口下阶的法器，在她手里，剑尖递出去，剑上那一道青气还要往前再走三尺，人在一丈开外，剑气已到了跟前。一剑一剑递过来，又快又稳，逼得台下的人屏住了气。头十招，她只使了五分力：一个四层，把卢方扔下了台，她要看看是怎么扔的。小满不看她的剑，看她的脚：剑往哪里去，脚先往哪里挪；脚往哪里挪，肩膀先往哪里沉。可她的脚，比卢方的干净得多，挪得又小又快，他看得见，身子总慢半步。第七招，剑尖挑破了他的袖子；第十五招，挑破了他的肩头；第二十招上，一道血口子从他右颊上拉过去，热乎乎的，淌进了领子里。他两只手里扣着诀，挡不得，只能躲，东一跳，西一滚，躲得极难看，有两回简直是连滚带爬。

可他没有乱躲。东一跳，西一滚，二十招里，他往台子的西北角上挪了七步。那一角的台沿上，有一摊红油，花椒粒子还粘在石缝里。

第二十二招上，秦雁握鞘的左手腾出两根指头，一掐，三根冰锥齐齐射了过来。小满一掌按在青石板上，身前拱起一片土墙，冰锥「噗噗噗」扎进土里；另一只手里已经冒出一团火，朝她脚底下打过去——她跳开的那一霎，他抢回了半步。台下有人叫起来：「两样！又是两样！」秦雁落了地，看了他一眼，那一眼里，是吃了一惊。

有一剑来得太快，他来不及看脚，只得往后一仰，剑尖贴着他的鼻子过去，削下了他额前的一绺头发。那绺头发在半空里飘啊飘，飘到台下，正落在阿禾的小本子上。阿禾低头看了一眼，把它夹进了本子里，面无表情。她拿笔的那只手，大拇指的指甲，一直掐在另一只手的掌心里。

可躲着躲着，小满觉出一样东西来，是他打记事起没有过的：他在笑。剑尖一回一回从他鼻子底下、耳朵边上过去，他浑身是口子，肋下那根骨头一喘一疼，嘴角却是往上的——这是头一回，对面站着一个比他强的人，一招一招都是真的，不藏，不让，不图他什么。他跟着那口剑转，像跟着爹在林子里追一头最好的鹿，追得心口发烫。台下的人起先屏着气，后来有人叫了一声好，再后来，一片一片地叫起来。

三十招上，他到底给逼到了台边——他自己挑的那一段台边。脚后跟底下，青石板只剩半寸，再往后，是冻土；左脚边上一尺，便是那摊油。秦雁的剑尖，抵在了他喉咙上，凉丝丝的。台下静了。

秦雁右手的袖子里，一直扣着一张黄纸雷符，符上的朱砂纹里有一线细细的蓝光游来游去，从第一招扣到这时候，始终没有掏出来。小满离她只有一剑远，看得见袖口里露出来的那一角。她往台下看了一眼：头一排蹲着几个刚进门的小孩子，正张着嘴看她，挤在台沿底下，离那几块青石板，不到一臂。那张符，她没有掏。小满的右手垂在袖子里，指头碰着了那三根痒痒针，碰了一碰，松开了。

她不用掏。剑尖抵在他喉咙上，她只要往前送一寸，他便只有往后退，一退，便下去了。阿禾那张纸上写的就是这一寸：两回大比，赢的四场，场场如此。这一寸要来，他早晨在灶口就知道了；拿什么去换，是他自己定的。

小满没有退。剑尖往前一送的那一霎，他往前迎了上去——身子一侧，让过喉咙，人贴着剑脊撞了进去。剑上那道青气从他左臂外侧犁过去，从肘弯一直犁到肩头，犁开一道口子，深的地方见了白，疼得他眼前白了一片；再偏半寸，这条胳膊便留在台上了。可他人已经到了秦雁跟前。三尺的剑气，到了一尺之内，使不开。他拿那只淌着血的左手，一把攥住了她左手里那截剑鞘。

秦雁一惊。剑在外头，回不来；她撒了鞘，左掌一翻，掌心里亮起一层青光——八层的一掌，贴着一个四层的胸口印实了，这个人往后便不用再修了。大比不许伤人性命。那层青光亮了一亮，她收了三分。

小满等的就是她收的这一下。人一收力，身子便往后脚上坐一坐；她的后脚边上，是那摊红油。他脚下一勾——猎户下套子勾兔子腿的那一下——勾的不是她站实了的那只脚，是另一只，把她往后带了半步。那一掌到底印了上来，只剩下三分，印在他胸口上，撞着一块硬东西，是烫的；他往后一屁股坐倒在台上，一口气半天没上来。

秦雁的脚跟，踩在了油上。八层的人，踩在冰上也站得住；可这一脚她正在收力，身子是松的，鞋底「哧」地一溜，溜出了台沿。她在半空里拧了一下腰，脚尖在台边上点了一点——点着的还是油——没点住。

她落在了台下的冻土上，站着落的，一步也没踉跄，剑还在手里。小满坐在台边上，左手攥着她那截剑鞘，血顺着鞘往下淌。那炷香，只剩一点红了。

执事咽了一口唾沫，敲锣：「……秦雁出台。沈小满，胜。」

台下先是一静，跟着便是一片吼声，比方才扔卢方的那一声还响，一浪一浪，从演武场这一头滚到那一头。

秦雁站在台下，低头看了看自己的手，又抬起头来看小满，看了好一会儿。小满爬起来，把那截剑鞘双手递了下去，压低了声音：「师姐。」秦雁接过鞘，抬起脚，看了看鞋底那一层红油，又看了看台沿上那一摊，道：「你是把我往那摊油上领的。」小满道：「……是，师姐。」秦雁道：「你是从第几招起，往那边领的？」小满道：「从头一招起。」她看了他一会儿，低声道：「四层的人，躲不过我三十招。你那双眼睛，不是练出来的。」小满道：「师姐也是。那一掌，师姐收了。」他看了一眼她的袖口。秦雁的眉毛轻轻一挑，拿左手把袖口按了一按，没接这话，只道：「收了三分。不收，你这会儿不在台上，在丹房。」又道：「往油上领人——猎户的套子。」小满一怔：「师姐怎么知道？」秦雁道：「我爹也是打猎的。我这个名字，就是他起的——他说雁是天上最难射的东西，一辈子没射着过一只。」她说着，竟笑了一笑，「他要是看见今天这一场，准说：那小子，拿一条胳膊换一只雁。」

执事唱了一声：「秦雁，负。」三回大比，三回都是这一个字。台下有人叹了口气。人堆里一个嗓子：「你……你把秦师姐打下去了？」是孙二狗。他脸色发白，「那半块干粮……我还没还她。」小满站在台边，左臂上的血顺着指尖往下滴，一句话也答不上来。秘境里伸进坑里拉他上来的，就是方才递回去的那一截剑鞘。

她转身要走，又停住了，背对着他，声音压得低低的：「四强，你跟马小宝一个半边。你怀里揣着的，不管是什么，捂紧了。」

老槐树底下，钱掌柜拿炭条把木板上的名字划得只剩几行：**祁长松　一赔一。马小宝　一赔四。**内门那个七层，一赔三。沈小满那一行，他把「二十」抹了，写上一个「五」。有人挤上来嚷：「掌柜的，我晌午押的是二十！」钱掌柜眼皮也不抬：「押出去的，照押出去的算。」
story_full.en:
This bout was nothing like the one before. Qin Yan's sword was a real sword and her moves were real moves. It was a magic tool of the lower grade, and in her hand, when the point went out, a streak of green qi on the blade went on another three feet; you could be ten feet away and the sword qi was already at you. Thrust after thrust came in, quick and steady, and below the stage people held their breath. For the first ten moves she used only half her strength: a fourth layer had thrown Lu Fang off the stage, and she wanted to see how. Xiaoman didn't watch her sword. He watched her feet: wherever the sword went, the feet moved there first; wherever the feet moved, the shoulder sank there first. But her feet were far cleaner than Lu Fang's, moving small and fast; he could see them, but his body was always half a step slow. At the seventh move the point slit his sleeve; at the fifteenth it slit his shoulder; at the twentieth a cut ran across his right cheek, hot, trickling down into his collar. His two hands were holding signs, so he couldn't block, only dodge, jumping this way, rolling that, dodging very uglily; twice it was little short of scrambling on all fours.

But he wasn't dodging at random. A jump this way, a roll that, and in twenty moves he had worked seven steps towards the north-west corner of the stage. On the stage's edge at that corner was a slick of red oil, Sichuan peppercorns still stuck in the cracks.

At the twenty-second move, Qin Yan freed two fingers of the left hand that held her scabbard and pinched, and three ice spikes shot at him together. Xiaoman slapped a palm onto the bluestone and a patch of earth wall heaved up in front of him; the ice spikes went *thup thup thup* into the earth. In his other hand a ball of fire had already come up, and he threw it at her feet; in the instant she jumped clear, he won back half a step. Someone below cried out: "Two! Two again!" Qin Yan landed and gave him one look, and in that look was surprise.

One thrust came too fast for him to watch the feet, and he could only lean back; the point passed along his nose and sheared off a lock of hair from his forehead. The lock of hair floated and floated in mid-air, floated down off the stage, and landed right on Ahe's little notebook. Ahe glanced down, tucked it into the notebook, her face blank. On the hand that held the pen, the thumbnail had been digging into the palm of her other hand all along.

But dodging and dodging, Xiaoman felt something he had never had since he could remember: he was smiling. Time after time the point went past under his nose, past his ear; he was cut all over, the bone in his side hurt with every breath, but the corners of his mouth turned up. This was the first time someone stronger than him stood facing him, every move real, nothing hidden, nothing given way, wanting nothing from him. He turned with that sword like following his father through the woods after the finest deer, following till his chest burned. At first the people below held their breath; later someone shouted "Good!", and later still it came in shout after shout.

At the thirtieth move he was forced at last to the stage's edge. The stretch of edge he had chosen himself. Under his heels there was half an inch of bluestone left; further back was frozen earth; a foot from his left foot was that slick of oil. The point of Qin Yan's sword rested against his throat, cool. Below, everything went quiet.

Up the right sleeve of Qin Yan's robe, all this time, she had been holding a yellow paper thunder talisman; in the cinnabar lines of it a thin thread of blue light wandered to and fro. She had held it from the first move to now and never brought it out. Xiaoman was only a sword's length from her and could see its corner at her cuff. She looked down off the stage: crouched in the front row were a few small children just come into the sect, watching her open-mouthed, squeezed in under the stage's edge, less than an arm's length from those bluestone slabs. She didn't bring that talisman out. Xiaoman's right hand hung in his sleeve, and his fingers touched the three Tickle Needles, touched them once, and let them go.

She didn't need to bring it out. With the point against his throat, she had only to push one inch forward, and he could only step back; and one step back, he was off. That one inch was what Ahe's paper said: in two contests, four bouts won, every one of them like this. He had known at the stove that morning this inch was coming; what to trade for it, he had decided himself.

Xiaoman didn't step back. In the instant the point pushed forward, he went forward to meet it: body turned sideways to let it past his throat, he drove in along the flat of the blade. The green qi on the sword ploughed along the outside of his left arm, from the crook of the elbow right up to the shoulder, ploughed open a gash, and where it was deepest the white showed; the pain turned everything in front of him white. Half an inch further over and that arm would have stayed on the stage. But he was already right in front of Qin Yan. Three feet of sword qi, inside a foot, has no room to work. With his bleeding left hand, he seized the length of scabbard in her left hand.

Qin Yan started. The sword was out there and couldn't come back. She let go of the scabbard and turned her left palm up, and a layer of green light lit in it. An eighth layer's palm, pressed home flat against a fourth layer's chest, and the boy would never cultivate again. The contest forbade taking life. The green light flared once, and she held back three tenths.

That holding back was what Xiaoman had been waiting for. When someone holds back their strength, their body settles back onto the rear foot; and beside her rear foot was that slick of red oil. His foot hooked out (the move a hunter uses to hook a hare's leg into a snare), and what it hooked wasn't the foot she stood solid on but the other one, drawing her back half a step. The palm did land in the end, with only three tenths left, pressed onto his chest, and struck something hard there that was hot. He sat down backwards on the stage, and for a long moment couldn't get his breath.

Qin Yan's heel came down on the oil. An eighth layer could stand on ice; but in this step she was just holding back her strength, her body loose, and her sole went skidding, *tsss*, off the edge of the stage. In mid-air she twisted at the waist and touched her toe to the edge of the stage. What it touched was oil again. It didn't hold.

She landed on the frozen ground below the stage, landed standing, not one stagger, sword still in hand. Xiaoman sat at the stage's edge with her length of scabbard in his left hand, blood running down it. Of the incense stick there was only a speck of red left.

The steward swallowed and struck the gong: "...Qin Yan is off the stage. Shen Xiaoman wins."

First a hush below, then a great roar, louder than the one when Lu Fang went off, wave on wave rolling from one end of the training ground to the other.

Qin Yan stood below the stage, looked down at her own hands, then looked up at Xiaoman for a good while. Xiaoman got up and handed the length of scabbard down to her with both hands, his voice low: "Senior Sister." Qin Yan took the scabbard, lifted her foot and looked at the layer of red oil on her sole, then at the slick on the stage's edge, and said: "You led me onto that oil." Xiaoman said: "...Yes, Senior Sister." Qin Yan said: "From which move did you start leading me there?" Xiaoman said: "From the first." She looked at him a while and said low: "A fourth layer can't dodge me for thirty moves. Those eyes of yours weren't trained." Xiaoman said: "Nor were yours, Senior Sister. That palm. You held it back." He glanced at her cuff. Qin Yan's eyebrows lifted slightly. She pressed her cuff down with her left hand and didn't take that up, only said: "Held back three tenths. If I hadn't, you wouldn't be on the stage now, you'd be in the pill house." Then she said: "Leading someone onto oil. A hunter's snare." Xiaoman started: "How do you know, Senior Sister?" Qin Yan said: "My pa's a hunter too. He gave me my name. He says the wild goose is the hardest thing in the sky to shoot, and he never shot one in his life." As she said it, she actually smiled. "If he'd seen this bout today, he'd say for sure: that lad traded an arm for a goose."

The steward called out: "Qin Yan, defeated." Three contests, and all three times this same word. Someone below sighed. A voice in the crowd: "You... you knocked Senior Sister Qin off?" It was Sun Ergou. His face had gone white. "That half piece of ration... I haven't paid her back yet." Xiaoman stood at the stage's edge, the blood from his left arm dripping off his fingertips, and couldn't find a word to answer. In the secret realm, what had reached down into the pit to pull him up was the very length of scabbard he'd just handed back.

She turned to go, then stopped, her back to him, her voice pitched low: "Last four, you and Ma Xiaobao are in the same half. Whatever it is you've got in your robe, keep a tight hold of it."

Under the old pagoda tree, Shopkeeper Qian had crossed out names on the board with his charcoal until only a few lines were left: **Qi Changsong · evens. Ma Xiaobao · four to one.** The inner-sect seventh layer, three to one. On Shen Xiaoman's line he rubbed out "twenty" and wrote a "five." Somebody pushed up shouting: "Shopkeeper, I bet at twenty at noon!" Shopkeeper Qian didn't lift an eyelid: "What's been bet goes at what it was bet at."
